title: Seeing images and using AI safely · Level 2
slo: Distinguish major computer-vision tasks and explain the purpose of AI guardrails.

exercises.question_text: A system that produces comprehensive image descriptions from visual features and associated text is a ___.

parts.text: A system that produces comprehensive image descriptions from visual features and associated text is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would not name the model type that integrates both modalities.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use multi-modal model when visual features and text descriptions are combined.

exercises.explanation: A multi-modal model combines visual features with associated text descriptions.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the task, its labeled images, and what it learns.

exercises.correct_answer: Image classification uses labeled images to learn the main subject
exercises.explanation: The sentence describes the training method before the learning target.

exercises.question_text: A photo-service designer needs detailed written image descriptions that use image features and related text. Which model should the designer choose?

options.rationale: A multi-modal model combines visual features and associated text descriptions. It is designed for comprehensive image descriptions.
Image classification gives a main-subject label. It cannot provide the requested detailed written description.
options.better_fit: Use it when one main-subject label is sufficient.

feedback.intrinsic: Users would receive only a label.
feedback.instructional: Use a multi-modal model for comprehensive descriptions.

options.rationale: Object detection provides locations of specific objects. It does not generate detailed written descriptions.
options.better_fit: Use it when object positions are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The service could locate objects without describing them.
feedback.instructional: Descriptions combining image and text features require a multi-modal model.

options.rationale: Semantic segmentation identifies individual pixels belonging to objects. It does not combine visual features with associated text.
options.better_fit: Use it when exact object boundaries are required.

feedback.intrinsic: The service would receive boundaries instead of descriptions.
feedback.instructional: Multi-modal models support detailed written image descriptions.

exercises.explanation: Correct—the design calls for a multi-modal model.

exercises.question_text: A retail catalog manager needs one label for every product photo, such as “shoe” or “bag.” Which choices fit the manager's goal? Select all that apply.

options.text: Train with product photos labeled by subject.
options.rationale: Classification training uses images labeled by their main subject. Product categories provide suitable labels.

options.text: Predict one subject label for each new photo.
options.rationale: The manager needs a main-subject label for each photo. This is the expected classification output.

options.text: Draw a box around each product.
options.rationale: Boxes communicate object locations, which is object detection. The stated outcome is a label, not a position.
options.better_fit: Use it when product locations in a multi-item photo matter.

feedback.intrinsic: This adds locations instead of the requested label.
feedback.instructional: A single product label calls for image classification.

options.rationale: Pixel-level identification is semantic segmentation. It exceeds the manager's need for a category label.
options.better_fit: Use it when exact product boundaries are required.

exercises.explanation: Correct—the goal is labeled product photos.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The purpose of guardrails is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the approach, then the guardrails and their purpose.

exercises.correct_answer: Responsible AI uses guardrails to reduce risk from harmful actions
exercises.explanation: The sentence connects responsible AI, guardrails, and their risk-reduction purpose.

exercises.question_text: AI systems trained to analyze photographs, videos, and camera feeds use ___.

parts.text: AI systems trained to analyze photographs, videos, and camera feeds use

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would not name the visual-analysis field.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use computer vision for AI that analyzes visual input.

exercises.explanation: Computer vision is the AI field concerned with visual input.

exercises.question_text: A product manager is designing an AI assistant that could generate harmful replies. Which actions should the manager choose? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Content filters are a safeguard that can reduce harmful generated content. They directly address part of the stated risk.
Responsible AI requires guardrails from conception through design, implementation, and operation. Considering them during design is necessary.

options.text: Wait until operation to consider risks.
options.rationale: Waiting until operation ignores the need to consider risks from conception onward. It can allow preventable risks into the system.
options.better_fit: No responsible-AI scenario supports delaying all risk work until operation.

feedback.intrinsic: Avoidable harmful replies may reach users first.

options.rationale: Content filters reduce one category of risk but do not make a system wholly responsible. Broader lifecycle guardrails remain necessary.
options.better_fit: Use filters as one component of a broader safeguard strategy.

feedback.instructional: Responsible AI requires more than filters alone.

exercises.explanation: Correct—use content filters and lifecycle-wide guardrails.

exercises.question_text: A museum app must analyze visitor-uploaded photos, identify vintage computers, and describe what it sees. Which capability should the curator choose?

options.rationale: Computer vision analyzes visual input and can identify and describe uploaded images. It matches the museum app's image-based goal.
Information extraction is for pulling targeted details from content. The app needs broader analysis and description of a photograph.
options.better_fit: Use it when extracting a serial number shown in an image.

feedback.intrinsic: The app could miss the overall visual description.
feedback.instructional: Use computer vision for broad visual analysis.

options.rationale: Text classification assigns categories to written text. The curator's primary input is photographs.
options.better_fit: Use it when classifying written visitor reviews.

feedback.intrinsic: The photos would not be analyzed as visual input.
feedback.instructional: This decision concerns images, so choose computer vision.

options.rationale: Speech recognition converts spoken audio to text. It does not analyze uploaded photographs.
options.better_fit: Use it to transcribe visitors' spoken questions.

feedback.instructional: Computer vision handles images and video.

exercises.question_text: To find specific items and report their positions in an image, use ___.

parts.text: To find specific items and report their positions in an image, use

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would either label an image broadly or identify pixels.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use object detection for specific items and their positions.

exercises.explanation: Object detection identifies particular objects and reports where they are.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the two tasks is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with semantic segmentation, then state that it extends object detection.

exercises.correct_answer: Semantic segmentation is an advanced form of object detection with pixel-level detail
exercises.explanation: The sentence explains segmentation's relationship to object detection and its higher level of detail.

exercises.question_text: A store manager uses shelf-camera images and needs to know where each item is on a shelf. Which task should the manager choose?

options.rationale: The manager needs locations for specific shelf items. Object detection provides those locations.
Classification gives one main-subject label for an image. It cannot show each item's shelf position.
options.better_fit: Use it when a photo needs one overall label.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would not see item positions.
feedback.instructional: When locations matter, use object detection.

options.rationale: Segmentation identifies individual pixels belonging to objects. The manager needs positions, not exact pixel boundaries.
options.better_fit: Use it when precise item boundaries are required.

feedback.intrinsic: This provides finer detail than the shelf-monitoring decision requires.
feedback.instructional: Object detection is the appropriate location-focused task.

options.rationale: Text summarization condenses written material. It cannot identify objects in shelf-camera images.
options.better_fit: Use it to condense a written stock report.

feedback.intrinsic: The shelf images would not yield item locations.
feedback.instructional: Choose a computer-vision task for image input.

exercises.question_text: A robotics engineer must isolate an object's exact boundary in an image before the robot grasps it. Which choices fit this need? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Semantic segmentation supplies pixel-level object information. That detail supports identifying an exact boundary.
Individual pixels define the object boundary in the image. This is the required segmentation output.

options.text: Use image classification for one label.
options.rationale: Classification supplies one main-subject label. It does not reveal an object's exact boundary.
options.better_fit: Use it when only the image's main subject matters.

feedback.intrinsic: The robot would have a label but no grasp boundary.

options.text: Use object detection for only a box.
options.rationale: A location box can include pixels outside an object. The engineer needs the exact boundary instead.
options.better_fit: Use it when an approximate object location is enough.

feedback.intrinsic: The grasp area could include background pixels.
feedback.instructional: Use segmentation when individual pixels are required.
